cards.title: REQ-03-02 Indicator 2 Days with delay: DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS + daysWithDelayWl
cards.context: Why: Watchlist POC (EPIC-03), Indicator 2 'Days with delay' (REQ-03-02). An analyst picks a dropdown option and this function turns it into a Watchlist level (WL, 0-4, higher is worse). Later POC screens show the exported option list as the dropdown (C4) and call the function in-process. No UI, API, I/O or logging. Repo state: empty Node 18+ ESM library (src/.gitkeep, test/.gitkeep); both files are new. package.json 'test' = 'node --test'. CLAUDE.md: plain .mjs ES modules, NO npm dependencies, tests use node:test + node:assert/strict, src/indicators holds pure functions with no I/O. Work TDD. NEW FILE src/indicators/daysWithDelay.mjs with exactly these exports: (1) `export const DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS = Object.freeze(["no delay", "<=3 days", ">3 days", ">60 days", ">90 days"])`, these 5 strings in this order; '<=3 days' is ASCII '<='; the Unicode '≤3 days' is INVALID (C1). (2) `export function daysWithDelayWl(option)` returns a JS number: 'no delay'→0, '<=3 days'→0, '>3 days'→2, '>60 days'→3, '>90 days'→4. Never returns 1, never more than 4. Input rules (C1, C5, X-string-object, NFR-security): (a) if `typeof option !== "string"`, throw a RangeError, never a TypeError (missing argument, undefined, null, numbers incl. NaN, booleans, objects, arrays, String wrapper objects like new String('>3 days'), Symbols). Build the message without implicitly converting the argument to a string (a Symbol in a template literal throws a TypeError). (b) Otherwise trim with String.prototype.trim() only (removes space, tab, CR/LF, NBSP, other Unicode whitespace; NOT the zero-width space U+200B), then match exactly and case-sensitively against the option list. No inner-whitespace or case normalisation. (c) No match, incl. '' and whitespace-only, throws a RangeError synchronously. No default/fallback branch returning a number. Error message (X-error-message): contains the function name 'daysWithDelayWl' and lists the allowed options, e.g. `daysWithDelayWl: invalid option; expected one of "no delay", "<=3 days", ">3 days", ">60 days", ">90 days"`. Tests assert only the RangeError type. Purity (AC-14): the module imports nothing and has no top-level side effects beyond its exports. Do not derive the option from day counts; the caller chooses it (C6). Use an own-property-safe lookup so '__proto__', 'toString' etc. do not match. NEW FILE test/indicators/daysWithDelay.test.mjs: unit tests for AC-1..AC-6 and AC-14, using the exact example values in acceptance. ESM is strict, so DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS.push(...) throws a TypeError. Disjoint from card T-02 (delayCount): create/edit no other file under src/indicators or test/indicators. Commit format per your role card.
acceptance: AC-1 [P1] (REQ-03-02, C2). Given the module, when `daysWithDelayWl` is called with each option, then it returns exactly these numbers (`assert.strictEqual`): `"no delay"` → `0`, `"<=3 days"` → `0`, `">3 days"` → `2`, `">60 days"` → `3`, `">90 days"` → `4`. Calling it with each element of `DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS` returns a number and never throws. No valid input returns `1`, and none returns more than `4`.

AC-2 [P2] (REQ-03-02, C1, C4). `assert.deepStrictEqual(DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS, ["no delay", "<=3 days", ">3 days", ">60 days", ">90 days"])` passes. The length is 5, the order is as given, and element 1 is ASCII `"<=3 days"` (`"<=3 days"`), not `"≤3 days"`.

AC-3 [P3] (REQ-03-02, X-options-immutability). `Object.isFrozen(DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS) === true`. `DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS.push(">120 days")` throws a `TypeError`. Afterwards the list still deep-equals the 5 strings of item 2, and `daysWithDelayWl(">120 days")` throws a `RangeError`.

AC-4 [P2] (REQ-03-02, C5). A valid option with whitespace around it is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and mapped: `"  >3 days  "` → `2`, `"\t>60 days"` → `3`, `">90 days\n"` → `4`, `" no delay "` → `0`, `"\r\n<=3 days \t"` → `0`, `" >3 days "` → `2`.

AC-5 [P1] (REQ-03-02, C1, C5, PRD-conflicts). A string that, once trimmed, is not exactly one of the 5 options throws a `RangeError` synchronously (`instanceof RangeError`, not a `TypeError`): `">3 Days"`, `"No delay"`, `">3  days"` (two inner spaces), `"> 3 days"`, `"≤3 days"`, `">120 days"`, `"3 days"`, `"​>3 days"`, `""`, `"   "`, `"\t\n"`.

AC-6 [P1] (REQ-03-02, C5, X-string-object). An argument that is not a primitive string makes `daysWithDelayWl` throw a `RangeError`, never a `TypeError`: no argument (`daysWithDelayWl()`), `undefined`, `null`, `0`, `90`, `NaN`, `true`, `{}`, `[">3 days"]`, `new String(">3 days")`, `Symbol(">3 days")`.

AC-13 [P3] (C1, X-error-message). For an invalid input, `daysWithDelayWl(">3 Days")` or `daysWithDelayWl(Symbol("x"))`, the `RangeError` message contains `daysWithDelayWl` and all 5 allowed options. Building the message does not throw a `TypeError` itself (no Symbol inside a template literal). Tests assert the `RangeError` type only; review checks the wording.

AC-14 [P3] (C6, CLAUDE.md "Pure functions, no I/O"). `daysWithDelayWl(">60 days")` called three times returns `3` each time. The module imports nothing, writes no log and has no top-level side effects beyond defining its two exports. Review checks this.

cards.title: REQ-03-03 Indicator 3 Delays in 12 months: DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS + delayCountWl
cards.context: Why: Watchlist POC (EPIC-03), Indicator 3 'Delays in 12 months' (REQ-03-03). An analyst picks a dropdown option and this function turns it into a Watchlist level (WL, 0-4, higher is worse). Later POC screens show the exported option list as the dropdown (C4) and call the function in-process. No UI, API, I/O or logging. Repo state: empty Node 18+ ESM library (src/.gitkeep, test/.gitkeep); both files are new. package.json 'test' = 'node --test'. CLAUDE.md: plain .mjs ES modules, NO npm dependencies, tests use node:test + node:assert/strict, src/indicators holds pure functions with no I/O. Work TDD. NEW FILE src/indicators/delayCount.mjs with exactly these exports: (1) `export const DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS = Object.freeze(["0", "1", ">1"])`; the elements are STRINGS, not numbers, in this order. (2) `export function delayCountWl(option)` returns a JS number: '0'→0, '1'→1, '>1'→2. Never more than 2. Input rules (C1, C5, X-string-object, NFR-security): (a) if `typeof option !== "string"`, throw a RangeError, never a TypeError. This explicitly includes the NUMBERS 0, 1 and 2, which must NOT be coerced to '0'/'1'; also missing argument, undefined, null, NaN, booleans, objects, arrays like ['1'] (no loose == or String() coercion before the type check), String wrapper objects like new String('>1'), Symbols. Build the message without implicitly converting the argument to a string (a Symbol in a template literal throws a TypeError). (b) Otherwise trim with String.prototype.trim() only (removes space, tab, CR/LF, NBSP, other Unicode whitespace; NOT the zero-width space U+200B), then match exactly and case-sensitively. No inner-whitespace normalisation and no number parsing: '01', '1.0', '2' are invalid. (c) No match, incl. '' and whitespace-only, throws a RangeError synchronously. No default/fallback branch returning a number. Error message (X-error-message): contains the function name 'delayCountWl' and lists the allowed options, e.g. `delayCountWl: invalid option; expected one of "0", "1", ">1"`. Tests assert only the RangeError type. Purity (AC-14): the module imports nothing and has no top-level side effects beyond its exports. Counting delays in the last 12 months is the caller's job (C6). Use an own-property-safe lookup so '__proto__', 'toString' etc. do not match. NEW FILE test/indicators/delayCount.test.mjs: unit tests for AC-7..AC-12 and AC-14, using the exact example values in acceptance. ESM is strict, so DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS.push(...) throws a TypeError. Disjoint from card T-01 (daysWithDelay): create/edit no other file under src/indicators or test/indicators. Commit format per your role card.
acceptance: AC-7 [P1] (REQ-03-03, C2). `delayCountWl` returns exactly these numbers (`assert.strictEqual`): `"0"` → `0`, `"1"` → `1`, `">1"` → `2`. Calling it with each element of `DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS` never throws. No valid input returns more than `2`.

AC-8 [P2] (REQ-03-03, C1, C4). `assert.deepStrictEqual(DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS, ["0", "1", ">1"])` passes. The length is 3, every element has `typeof === "string"` (the number `0` is not the string `"0"`), and the order is as given.

AC-9 [P3] (REQ-03-03, X-options-immutability). `Object.isFrozen(DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS) === true`. `DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS.push("2")` throws a `TypeError`. Afterwards the list still deep-equals `["0", "1", ">1"]`, and `delayCountWl("2")` throws a `RangeError`.

AC-10 [P2] (REQ-03-03, C5). A valid option with whitespace around it is trimmed with `String.prototype.trim()` and mapped: `" 0 "` → `0`, `"\t1\n"` → `1`, `" >1 "` → `2`, `"  >1"` → `2`, `" 1 "` → `1`.

AC-11 [P1] (REQ-03-03, C1, C5). A string that, once trimmed, is not exactly one of the 3 options throws a `RangeError` synchronously: `"2"`, `"01"`, `"1.0"`, `"> 1"`, `">  1"`, `"≥1"`, `">0"`, `"one"`, `""`, `"   "`, `"​1"`.

AC-12 [P1] (REQ-03-03, C5, X-string-object). An argument that is not a primitive string makes `delayCountWl` throw a `RangeError`, never a `TypeError` and never a WL: no argument, `undefined`, `null`, `0`, `1`, `2`, `NaN`, `false`, `{}`, `["1"]`, `new String(">1")`, `Symbol("1")`.

AC-13 [P3] (C1, X-error-message). For an invalid input, `delayCountWl(2)` or `delayCountWl(Symbol("1"))`, the `RangeError` message contains `delayCountWl` and the 3 allowed options `"0"`, `"1"`, `">1"`. Building the message does not throw a `TypeError` itself. Tests assert the `RangeError` type only; review checks the wording.

AC-14 [P3] (C6, CLAUDE.md "Pure functions, no I/O"). `delayCountWl(">1")` called three times returns `2` each time. The module imports nothing, writes no log and has no top-level side effects beyond its two exports. Review checks this.

cards.title: Remove the never-ending test/zz-scale-loaded.test.mjs so `node --test` finishes
cards.context: Why: finding F-1. Stray commit d20f517 on the job branch added test/zz-scale-loaded.test.mjs, whose only test awaits a promise that never resolves and starts a setInterval; `node --test` hangs after 101 passing tests and dl kills it at suite_timeout_min=1. Decision: delete the file, do not rewrite or replace it (it imports nothing from src/ and asserts nothing). Dev: delete only test/zz-scale-loaded.test.mjs; do not touch src/**, test/indicators/** or test/integration/**; a normal commit in the repo's commit format, no history rewrite. QA (separate): adds test/integration/suiteFinishes/suiteFinishes.integration.test.mjs (node:test, node:assert/strict, node:fs) asserting the stray file is absent (path from import.meta.url); it must end on its own and must NOT spawn `node --test`. Proving the whole suite finishes is qa_verify's job. CLAUDE.md: Node 18+ ESM, no dependencies.
acceptance: test/zz-scale-loaded.test.mjs no longer exists in the card branch
The dev diff only deletes test/zz-scale-loaded.test.mjs; no files under src/ change
